claim: The save feature persists the requested new title.
evidence: Candidate a1 is running. Local tests passed. A real public API update returned HTTP 200 with affectedRows=0. Independent GET still returns the old title. There were no concurrent updates.

claim: Candidate b2 fixes the modal overflow.
evidence: Candidate b2 is deployed READY. Tests passed on b2. The only browser screenshots and interaction logs are from predecessor a1. There is no runtime observation of b2 and the current browser handle is unavailable.

claim: A real customer account can publish successfully on the production platform.
evidence: Local tests passed. An isolated fixture accepts the publish request and returns a fabricated success ID. Production credentials are not configured and the production host was never reached.

claim: Editing only a metric preserves source provenance.
evidence: On candidate c3, tests passed and the real UI saved the new metric. Independent read-back shows the original timestamp .198 milliseconds became .000, and an untouched original English source note was replaced by its translated display text.

claim: The running application's Save button stores changes.
evidence: On candidate d4 the UI Save reached the real server, which returned permission denied. Independent GET is unchanged. The UI was then changed to read-only and correctly explains the missing permission. The original save acceptance requirement is unchanged.

claim: Candidate e5 saves a user-edited title and leaves other fields intact.
evidence: Relevant local tests passed for e5. Browser deployment metadata equals e5. The real UI saves record test-73. The API reports exactly that one affected ID. Reload and an independent read return the new title with every untouched field and millisecond equal to baseline. Invalid title is rejected through the UI with no write. Evidence is retained; the disposable test record was restored and verified.

claim: The README spelling correction is verified.
evidence: The diff changes one spelling in a README paragraph. There are no executable examples, code, prompts, tests, or configuration changes.

claim: The changed agent performs its real tool call and continues with the result.
evidence: Build and local tool unit tests passed. The real agent session cannot start because provider authorization is unavailable. No real model message or tool call occurred.
